variants.name: Live signal: KLCI, ringgit, MGS 10Y trend, MGS–UST spread
US 10Y trend in place of the MGS trend
Korea-style rotation (KLCI inverted: stocks down = bonds up)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Kuala Lumpur close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Kuala Lumpur). Hedged = MGS 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the MGS 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (^KLSE) and USD/MYR (MYR=X) daily closes; any USD/MYR close more than 1.5% from BNM’s KL USD/MYR reference rate is replaced by it. MGS 10Y and 15Y: BNM FAST consolidated indicative yield-to-maturity. US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/MYR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker ringgit is bond-bearish)
MGS − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: MGS − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: The KLCI falls 0.5% to 1,566.7, its lowest close since August 2025, and USD/MYR rises 0.55% to 4.1135 despite a Q3 GDP beat; the 10Y MGS still slips 1.2bp to 3.842%. Signal −0.53: bond sell-off, only just
notes.now: The KLCI fell 0.53% to 1,566.73 and is down 2.05% over 20 sessions while USD/MYR rose 0.83%; Bursa data show foreign funds net sold RM270.2m of shares in the week to Nov 13 and RM6.82bn this year, but BNM's October data had foreigners adding RM4.7bn of MGS to a record RM238.2bn, and who traded bonds today is not published. The daily signal is −0.53 (−0.47 yesterday, −0.75 20 sessions ago), just past the −0.5 sell-off line: the spread part is the most bearish (z −1.22), then the KLCI part (z −0.77) and the ringgit part (z +0.62 on USD/MYR, bond-bearish), while the 10Y trend part leans bond-bullish (z −0.49, the 10Y down 1.9bp over 20 sessions). MGS yield 125.8bp less than Treasuries, 27bp below the 130-day average gap and in the bottom 5% of the past year; that is a nominal gap before currency risk, and it says MGS are rich to Treasuries, not that foreigners are leaving. Overnight the US 10Y fell about 2bp to 5.10%, which at the one-year daily beta of 0.15 (correlation 0.34) implies −0.3bp for the 10Y MGS; it fell 1.2bp, so most of today's move was local, and the next-day spill-over beta is only 0.022. Over four weeks the 10Y MGS is down 3.8bp while the US 10Y rose 14bp; at a weekly beta of 0.32 the Treasury-linked part is +4.4bp and −8.2bp is local, the part Treasuries do not explain. As a cross-check, the FX swap prices ringgit at 2.84% for 1 month and 2.89% for 3 months, 9.0bp and 6.6bp under onshore rates, which fits steady demand to hold ringgit or dollar funding needs more than a rush out of the currency (first stored day, indicative levels). Since June 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 1.10 outright and 1.36 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 38.5% of the time over the next 20 sessions (44.3% hedged) and the 10Y fell 1.7bp on average after them, and since September 2024 the Sharpe is 0.49 outright and 0.27 hedged; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral to mildly long duration rather than short, because sell-off calls have had no edge and today's reading rests mostly on the rich MGS−UST gap.
notes.flip: The daily signal is −0.53, just below the −0.5 sell-off line. A return to neutral needs only a small change: a KLCI back above about 1,590, USD/MYR back under 4.08, or a Treasury rally that narrows the MGS−UST gap toward its 130-day average. A deeper sell-off would come from a KLCI break below 1,550, USD/MYR above 4.15 or the 10Y MGS back above 3.90%. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a KLCI rebound with foreign buying and a firmer ringgit together, the pattern of late 2023 to 2024. Policy triggers are Malaysia's October CPI on Nov 19, the Fed's December decision (a hike is mostly priced) and any firmer BNM signal on a 2027 hike.
phases: KLCI 1,373–1,619 while the 10Y rose from 3.56% to 4.36% (peak 4.55%) and USD/MYR from 4.15 to 4.72; BNM began hiking in May 2022 as the Fed tightened.
BNM took the OPR to 3.00% in May 2023; KLCI 1,375–1,502, 10Y 3.65–4.50%, and USD/MYR peaked near 4.79 in October 2023 as US yields climbed.
KLCI from 1,435 to 1,649, 10Y from 4.07% to 3.71% and USD/MYR from 4.76 to 4.12: stocks, ringgit and bonds rallied together, the signal's best stretch (hedged Sharpe 2.24 from 2022 to August 2024).
KLCI fell to 1,401 on Apr 9, 2025 and USD/MYR reached 4.51, but the 10Y held 3.63–3.94%: MGS barely sold off with stocks.
BNM cut the OPR to 2.75% in July 2025; the 10Y fell to 3.36%, the KLCI hit 1,771 on Jan 27, 2026 and USD/MYR dipped to 3.88.

With the US 10Y above 5%, the 10Y MGS rose to 4.18% on Sep 11 before settling near 3.84%; the KLCI slid from 1,749 to 1,567 on AI-related selling and foreign outflows, and BNM held on Nov 5 with a hawkish tilt. MGS now yield about 126bp less than Treasuries.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign holdings of MGS/GII and Bursa foreign flows are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the KLCI and the ringgit stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/MYR is Yahoo's close, replaced by BNM's KL reference rate on any day it strays more than 1.5% (today 4.1135 against BNM's 4.1055 and FXEmpire's 4.116 spot, within 0.3%); the 10Y is FAST's indicative curve, and the 20-session windows count stored sessions. The daily back-test runs from June 24, 2022 (1,077 sessions): the live signal makes 135.7bp outright (Sharpe 1.10) and 142.4bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 1.36), against 36.1bp for always holding the 10Y (Sharpe 0.23); the weekly build scores 0.77 outright and 0.86 hedged, and its variants (adding the US 10Y trend 0.60, ringgit trend alone 0.35) were picked after the fact and are not live. FX-swap implied yields start on Nov 18, 2026. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
